newsitem.title: ITALY: Lauro hijacker to stand trial for prison evasion.
newsitem.headline: Lauro hijacker to stand trial for prison evasion.

text.p: A Palestinian who fled Italy while serving a prison term for the 1985 hijacking of the cruise ship Achille Lauro was ordered on Wednesday to stand trial, judicial officials said.
Magied al-Molqi will stand trial on September 22 for failing to return to Rome's Rebbibia jail after 12 days leave for good behaviour in February 1996.
He had been serving a 30-year prison term for hijacking the Italian liner off the Egyptian coast and killing a passenger.
Court sources said two other Palestinians would face charges of supplying money and false passports to help al-Molqi flee Italy.
He was arrested in southern Spain after a few weeks and extradited back to Italy in December 1996.

The United States had offered a $2 million reward for the capture of al-Molqi, who was held primarily responsible for the murder of Jewish-American passenger Leon Klinghoffer aboard the Achille Lauro.
The 67-year-old Klinghoffer had been shot and dumped overboard from his wheelchair during the hijacking, which al-Molqi carried out with three other guerrillas.
